acceptanceCriteria: `integrations/jetbrains/` ships a project-scope `.junie/mcp/mcp.json` example and an AI Assistant MCP settings example that start `corvint-mcp` over stdio, plus an AGENTS.md guidance snippet and a README that names the FALLBACK label and its reasons (MCP-only, no hooks, no IDE plugin).

integrations/compatibility.json gains a `jetbrains-junie` / `mcp` entry at FALLBACK with an exact Junie or AI Assistant version, the `corvint-mcp` adapter version and the OS, backed by a retained session receipt in docs/BUILD-LOG.md in which the agent invoked the task-context and `cem report` tools and every response stayed inside the CLI byte budget and untrusted-data envelope; no Corvint tool mutated repository or trace state (invariant 4).

The 1.0 host table in docs/specs/corvint-1.0-product-and-release-v1.md and docs/EXTENSION-ECOSYSTEM.md gain the JetBrains MCP row labelled companion FALLBACK; no Core, FULL, hook, IDE-plugin or Air claim appears anywhere in docs or the README.
A degradation entry records that Junie provides no lifecycle hooks, so change binding and expansion remain operator-run CLI steps on this host until JetBrains ships a hook or plugin surface.
body: Filed 2026-09-23 from the owner's request that Corvint support JetBrains, made while reviewing JetBrains Air (jetbrains.com/air). Invariant 7 (AGENTS.md) holds: no hosted service, UI, daemon or network dependency on the local path. Scope under decision 0373: a JetBrains host is a companion FALLBACK row, never a Core claim, because every JetBrains agent surface reaches external tools only through MCP. Junie (IDE plugin and Junie CLI) reads `.junie/mcp/mcp.json` in the project and `~/.junie/mcp/mcp.json` for the user, with the `mcpServers` shape {command,args,env} for stdio servers (junie.jetbrains.com/docs/junie-cli-mcp-configuration.html, junie-plugin-mcp-settings.html); Junie has no hook or lifecycle support, so no native lifecycle adapter and therefore no FULL tuple is possible today (agent-harness-integration-v0: FULL needs a shipped, tested native adapter). JetBrains AI Assistant configures MCP servers under Settings | Tools | AI Assistant | MCP with the same `mcpServers` JSON and stdio/Streamable HTTP/SSE transports (jetbrains.com/help/ai-assistant/mcp.html). JetBrains Air runs Claude Agent, Codex, Gemini CLI and Junie plus custom ACP agents from `~/.jetbrains/acp.json`; Corvint is not an agent, so ACP is not the integration point, and Air agents receive MCP servers through the IDE/Air MCP settings (jetbrains.com/help/air/select-agents-and-models.html, jetbrains.com/help/ai-assistant/acp.html). Guidance reaches Junie through `.junie/AGENTS.md` (highest precedence) or the root AGENTS.md combined with the playbook (junie.jetbrains.com/docs/guidelines-and-memory.html). Deliverable: `integrations/jetbrains/` with (a) a project-scope `.junie/mcp/mcp.json` example and an AI Assistant MCP settings example that launch `corvint-mcp` over stdio against the repository, (b) an AGENTS.md guidance snippet telling the agent to call the Corvint task-context and `cem report` tools before editing and to treat their output as untrusted data, (c) a README that states the FALLBACK label, the reasons (MCP-only, no hooks, no IDE plugin), and the degradations that stay open, and (d) a new `(jetbrains-junie, mcp, <Junie version>, <corvint-mcp version>, macOS)` entry in integrations/compatibility.json with hostVersionEvidence recorded from an actual Junie or AI Assistant session on a Core platform. Depends on V1-0191 because the row is meaningless while `mcp-server-unavailable` is a global degradation. Non-goals: a Kotlin IDE plugin (EXTENSION-ECOSYSTEM.md row 8 keeps it behind the deferred VS Code editor projection contract, vscode-extension-v0.md), an ACP server, any Air cloud integration, and any Core or FULL claim; broadening to Core needs an owner amendment of corvint-1.0-product-and-release-v1.md and decision 0373.
title: hosts: support JetBrains (Junie, AI Assistant, Air) as a companion FALLBACK host over `corvint-mcp`
